mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.2% within a month indicates a tightening labor market, which can lead to increased wage pressures and inflation, causing the S&P 500 to experience negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (PCE) over three months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the signal is active.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% within a month indicates a surge in economic activity, which can lead to increased demand for equities, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts by more than 5% within a month signals a weakening in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of reduced consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds the CPI inflation rate by more than 1%, it indicates a real tightening of monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.1% within a month, it signals a strong labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.1% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP by more than 2% over a quarter signals strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
